ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.claim: The future success promised to the Prophet is followed by reminders of earlier deliverance and spiritual blessing, then guidance to fulfil the duties those favours impose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.anchor: At the end, he is guided to fulfil the obligations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r5.claim: The orphan example begins the proof from the Prophet’s own life that a future better than the present was possible; orphanhood was especially precarious in uncaring Arab society.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r5.anchor: First of all, a reference is given to him being an orphan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p359/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p359/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p359/r1.claim: Although Arab society often neglected orphans, God provided the Prophet affectionate care through his grandfather and uncle; Islahi compares this providence to Moses’ upbringing and cites 89:17 and 107:2 on orphan abuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p359/r1.anchor: his grandfather and after him, his paternal uncle brought him up with great respect and affection

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r10.claim: God sheltered the orphan Muhammad with his uncle Abu Talib; another reading says God nurtured him with care and brought him to an intimate station no one shared.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r10.anchor: قيل : إلى عمه أبي طالب . ويقال : بل آواه إلى كنف ظله

FARRA:v3p273#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r6.claim: Muḥammad was under Abū Ṭālib's care; God gave him shelter and relieved his need for Abū Ṭālib through contentment, not wealth.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r6.anchor: يقول: كنت في حجر أبي طالب، فجعل لك مأوى، وأغناك عنه، ولم يك غنى عن كثرة مال،

FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.claim: In fa-awā and fa-aghnā the understood second-person pronoun is omitted to match the verse endings.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.anchor: فجرى على طرح الكاف لمشاكلة رءوس الآيات.

BINTSHATI:v1p57/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p57/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v1p57/r1.claim: A report treats al-Sharh and al-Duha as one surah because both recount divine favors, including sheltering the orphan and expanding the Prophet's breast.
BINTSHATI:v1p57/r1.anchor: واقترنت بها في رواية تقول إن الضحى والشرح سورة واحدة لما يبدو من المناسبة

NAHHAS:v5p249/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r12.claim: The verb wajada takes two objects here and can mean to see or to know.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r12.anchor: مفعولا يجد ويجد في كلام العرب تنقسم أقساما منها أن يكون بمعنى يرى وتعلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r5.claim: The reminder of orphanhood refers to the Prophet losing his father and being raised under Abu Talib's care.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r5.anchor: ثم وقفه تعالى على المراتب التي رجه عنها بإنعامه ويتمه، كان فقد أبيه وكونه في كنف عمه أبي طالب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r6.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r6.claim: Asked why the Prophet was orphaned from both parents, Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says it was so no creature could claim a right over him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r6.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق لم يتم النبي عليه السلام من أبويه، فقال لئلا يكون عليه حق لمخلوق،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r7.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r7.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads fa-awa short, with the sense of showing mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي «فأوى» بالقصر بمعنى رحم، تقول أويت لفلان أي رحمته،

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r4.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r4.claim: He reads fa-awā with a short alif, meaning “he showed you mercy,” in contrast to the common long form.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r4.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: فأوى بالقصر أي: رحمك

MUQATIL:93:1-6/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r7.claim: God reminds Muhammad that He sheltered him as an orphan by placing him with his uncle Abu Talib, who provided for him.
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r7.anchor: { ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى } [آية: 6] يقول: فضمك إلى عمك أبي طالب، فكفاك المؤنة

ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r5.claim: The Prophet’s uncle Abū Ṭālib took care of him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r5.anchor: وكان النبي عليه السلام يكفله عمه أبو طالب

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah consoles the Prophet: it assures him God will not abandon him, recalls God's favors, and ends by urging care for the downtrodden and preaching the message.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.anchor: The main theme of the sūrah is consolation of the Prophet. It begins with an assertion that God would not abandon the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.claim: Linguistically, 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, with the construction also implied in 93:7–8.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.anchor: Linguistically 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, Did He not find thee . . ., which is also implied in 93:7–8.

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r7.claim: God's favors include caring for the Prophet after his father died before birth, his mother died when he was two, and his grandfather guardian died when he was eight, after which his uncle raised him.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r7.anchor: فقد مات أبوه وهو في بطن أمه ثم ماتت أمه وهو ابن سنتين

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r8.claim: Another interpretation understands “orphan” figuratively as a unique pearl without peer, whom people gathered around.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد باليتيم الوحيد الذي لا نظير له في الناس كما يقال در يتيم

TABATABAI:94:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet asked why earlier prophets were granted special powers; God answered by reminding him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, expanded his chest, and lifted his burden.
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r5.anchor: ما رواه ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله

THALABI:v10p224#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224#2/r4.speaker: النبي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p224#2/r4.claim: In a conversation with God, the Prophet recalls asking for worldly gifts given to earlier people; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan and provided guidance and sufficiency.
THALABI:v10p224#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أكن سألته

THALABI:v10p224#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p224#2/r5.claim: The Prophet was a poor, vulnerable orphan after both parents died and left no property or shelter; God gave him a home and placed him with his uncle Abu Talib, who raised and supported him.
THALABI:v10p224#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: ألم يجدك يتيما صغيرا فقيرا ضعيفا حين مات أبواك

THALABI:v10p225/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
THALABI:v10p225/r1.claim: He explains that the Prophet was orphaned so he would owe no creature a claim upon him.
THALABI:v10p225/r1.anchor: لم أوتم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبويه؟ فقال: لئلا يكون عليه حق لمخلوق

THALABI:v10p225/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r2.speaker: عبد الوهاب بن مجاهد عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p225/r2.claim: He explains yateem as something unique without equal, so the verse means God found Muhammad unparalleled in honor and virtue and drew him near.
THALABI:v10p225/r2.anchor: ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى: هو من أقوال العرب: درة يتيمة إذا لم يكن لها مثل

THALABI:v10p225/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r3.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
THALABI:v10p225/r3.claim: He reads fa-awā with a shortened form meaning God showed mercy; Arabic uses awā for showing mercy.
THALABI:v10p225/r3.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي فأوى بالقصر: أي رحمك

THALABI:v10p229/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p229/r5.claim: The final kāf is omitted from fa-awā and the two parallel verbs to match the verse endings; the intended meaning remains clear.
THALABI:v10p229/r5.anchor: وحذف الكاف من قوله فآوى وأختيها لمشاكلة رؤوس الآي، ولأن المعنى معروف

BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r2.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r2.claim: A unique pearl is the image: the Prophet had no equal in Quraysh's nobility, and God sheltered and protected him among his enemies.
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r2.anchor: وفي "الكشاف" ومن بديع التفاسير أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة

BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r7.claim: The author rejects their view: the first surah depicts the Prophet's distress from unbelievers, while this one describes an opened chest and comfort, so their states differ.
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r7.anchor: لأن تلك حال غتمامه عليه السلام بأذى الكفار فهي حال محنة وضيق

QASHANI:93:4-8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:4-8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:4-8/r3.claim: The orphan is the solitary person veiled by self-qualities from the true father, the Holy Spirit; God sheltered him in divine care, educated him, and made his father a guardian to teach and purify him.
QASHANI:93:4-8/r3.anchor: محجوبا بصفات النفس عن نور أبيك الحقيقي

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.claim: God sheltered the orphan through the Prophet, guided the lost through him, and enriched the needy through him; the Prophet was sought in pre-eternity and made an envoy to creation.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : معناه وجد اليتيم فآوى بك ، ووجد الضال فهدى بك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.claim: Finding follows seeking; the Prophet was the sought beloved in the outward sense.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : وجدك أي طلبت حتى وجدت ، والمطلوب هو المراد

SULAMI:v2p402/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.claim: The Prophet was hidden among Meccans and unrecognized as a prophet until God revealed him; through him the fortunate were guided and the wretched destroyed.
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : مستترا في أهل مكة لم يعرفك أحدا بالنبوة حتى اظهرك

SULAMI:v2p402/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r7.claim: Orphanhood means the Prophet had no equal in nobility and purpose, so God sheltered him to Himself.
SULAMI:v2p402/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : في قوله : ^ ( ووجدك يتيما ) ^ أي : واجدا الأمثل لك

SULAMI:v2p402/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.claim: Though his people did not know his worth, God singled him out with favors, revealed His hidden bounty, and made his standing among them manifest.
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ومن ضاله في قومه لا يعرفون مقداره فخصه بخصائص بره

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.claim: In a discussion of Abu Talib's poetry, Ibn Amr says Muhammad was already a noble master; he explains orphanhood as losing both parents and poverty as the limited wealth then held by Arabs.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.anchor: من طريق موسى بن علي بن رباح عن أبيه رضي الله عنه قال : كنت عند مسلمة بن مخلد وعنده عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts God's answer to his request for prophetic miracles: God reminded him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, enrichment, opening his chest, removing his burden, and raising his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.claim: The Prophet says that after he asked about miracles granted earlier prophets, God reminded him He had sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, opened his chest, and raised his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.claim: A report says God answered Muhammad's comparison with Abraham and Moses by recalling his own blessings, including raised remembrance, and saying that He had chosen him as a close friend.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة اني لم اكن سالته

TUSTARI:93:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:6/r1.claim: Being found an orphan means being solitary, and God sheltered the Prophet among his companions.
TUSTARI:93:6/r1.anchor: قال: يعني ألم يجدك فردا فآواك إلى أصحابك.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.claim: Conflicting occasion reports suggest narrators lacked clarity; Ibn Ashur supposes the second revelation pause lasted about twelve days, to give the Prophet respite and build capacity for revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.anchor: فالذي نظنه أن احتباس الوحي في هذه المرة كان لمدة نحو من اثني عشر يوما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.claim: He reconciles reports by proposing a first pause of forty days, a second of roughly twelve, and the present surah as the third revelation, when practice of arduous work develops; this also reconciles reports about al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.anchor: فيكون نزول سورة الضحى هو النزول الثالث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.claim: The object of qalaa is omitted because waddaka makes it clear, a verbal ellipsis also seen in the following verbs awa, hada, and aghna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.anchor: وحذف مفعول { قلى } لدلالة { ودعك } عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.claim: The childhood-care account proves the promise is certain: God's steady care from the Prophet's beginnings cannot be coincidence, and reassures believers while warning opponents that the promise will occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.anchor: استئناف مسوق مساق الدليل على تحقق الوعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.claim: The rhetorical question expects assent; wajada means encountered, takes one object, and yatiim, dallan, and aa'il are circumstantial states in an image of aid given to someone in distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري ، وفعل { يجدك } مضارع وجد بمعنى ألفى وصادف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r6.claim: An orphan is a child whose father has died; the Prophet's father died before his birth or very early in infancy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r6.anchor: واليتيم : الصبي الذي مات أبوه وقد كان أبو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.claim: The objects of awa, hada, and aghna are omitted because the preceding second-person pronoun supplies them; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.anchor: وحذفت مفاعيل { فآوى } ، { فهدى } ، { فأغنى } للعلم بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r1.claim: God sheltered the Prophet by placing him with his uncle Abu Talib, who took care of his needs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r1.anchor: جعل لك مأوى إذا ضمك إلى عمك أبي طالب فكفاك المؤونة قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r2.claim: God gave the Prophet a home of his own and made him independent of Abu Talib's guardianship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158/r2.anchor: جعل لك مأوى لنفسك أغناك عن كفالة أبي طالب قاله ابن السائب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r6.claim: Muhammad was orphaned before or shortly after birth, lost his mother at six, and passed from his grandfather's care at eight to Abu Talib, who protected him through his mission. After Abu Talib died, God brought him to the Ansar, who sheltered and defended him; this was divine protection and wise providence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r6.anchor: فأقدم عليه سفهاء قريش وجهالهم، فاختار الله له الهجرة من بين أظهرهم إلى بلد الأنصار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.claim: Qatada says orphanhood, being guided, and being provided for were the Prophet's circumstances before God sent him as a messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} قال: كانت هذه منازل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يبعثه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet recounting God's reminders that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, enriched him, expanded his chest, and raised his remembrance; he affirms each gift.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أكن سألته

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.claim: One explanation for the pause in revelation is that a puppy was in the Prophet's house; Gabriel said angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.anchor: وقيل: سبب احتباسه كون جرو في بيته، فلما نزل جبريل سأله عن تأخيره

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.claim: Another report links the revelation to the Prophet's words on the Night Journey about David receiving iron and Abraham receiving fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.anchor: وقيل: قال ليلة المعراج: سخرت الحديد لداود، والنار لإبراهيم

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.claim: The Prophet asked why Solomon and others received great gifts; God reminded him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him, and he affirmed each reminder.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: سألت ربي مسألة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r4.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r4.claim: After the Prophet cut his finger and recited a couplet about its blood and suffering for God, revelation paused for two or three nights; Umm Jamīl said his devil had left him, and Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā came.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r4.anchor: وعن جندب بن سفيان: رمي رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بحجر في أصبعه

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives twelve days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.anchor: فقيل: اثنا عشر يوما، عن ابن جريج.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives fifteen days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.anchor: وقيل: خمسة عشر يوما، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.claim: Another report gives twenty-five days without naming its transmitter.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.claim: Muqātil gives forty days as the duration of the revelation pause.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet told Gabriel he had missed him; Gabriel replied that he missed him more, but descends only when commanded by his Lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.anchor: قال له النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: قد اشتقت إليك، فقال: وأنا أشد شوقا إليك

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.claim: If a pause is established, it should be explained as serving a benefit; neglecting the formula of exception taught believers but could not delay their interests.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.anchor: والصحيح إن ثبت التأخير أن يقال: إنه تأخير للمصلحة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.claim: Stories that the Prophet asked for gifts during or after the Night Journey are unsound: he asks only with permission, and a permitted request must be answered.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.anchor: فأما ما ذكروا من سؤاله ليلة المعراج وبعده فغير صحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.claim: Recounting past blessings from upbringing prepares the Prophet to expect further favor without impatience or discouragement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.anchor: عدد عليه نعمه وأياديه ، وأنه لم يخله منها من أول تربيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r2.claim: Wajada here means knowledge: the Prophet was an orphan; his father died while he was a six-month fetus, his mother when he was eight, and Abu Talib raised him well.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى : ألم تكن يتيما ، وذلك أن أباه مات وهو جنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r3.claim: The unique-pearl interpretation, meaning the Prophet was without equal in Quraysh, is an eccentric interpretation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r3.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أنه من قولهم : ( درة يتيمة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r4.claim: The reading fa-awa can derive from sheltering or from a verb meaning showing compassion, as in a shepherd's expression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r4.anchor: وقرىء : ( فآوى ) عو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r6.claim: An orphan is one whose father has died; Muhammad lost both parents when young, was cared for by his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, then his uncle Abu Talib.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r7.claim: One interpretation is literal fatherlessness; shelter meant a home and a guardian after the deaths of Abdullah and Abd al-Muttalib.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r7.anchor: من أبويه , فعلى هذا في قوله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r8.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r8.claim: He identifies Abu Talib as the guardian who cared for and supported the Prophet after his father and grandfather died.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r8.anchor: بعد موت عبد الله وعبد المطلب , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r9.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r9.claim: He says God provided the Prophet a home of his own and made him independent of Abu Talib's care.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r9.anchor: وأغناك عن كفالة أبي طالب , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes yatim metaphorically as one of a kind, without equal or counterpart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r10.anchor: لا مثيل له ولا نظير , من قولهم درة يتيمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r11.claim: On the metaphorical reading, God sheltered him near Himself and selected him for the Messenger's office.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r12.claim: A further possibility is that God made him a refuge for orphans and caretaker of people after he had been an orphan and dependent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r12.anchor: بعد أن كنت يتيما , وكفيل الأنام بعد أن كنت مكفولا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#3/r1.claim: “Did He not find you” uses find in the sense of know, with the two following nouns as its objects; the Prophet was an orphan when his parents died, and his uncle Abu Talib took him in and raised him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#3/r1.anchor: وهو من الوجود الذى بمعنى العلم والمنصوبان مفعولاه والمعنى ألم تكن يتيما حين مات أبواك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r1.claim: The Prophet was an orphan because his father had died; God gave him refuge with his uncle Abu Talib, who cared for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r1.anchor: فقال: { ألم يجدك يتيما } لا أب لك قد مات أبوك. { فآوى } أي جعل لك مأوى

QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says the Prophet was orphaned by both parents so that no created being would have a claim over him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r2.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق: لم أوتم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أبويه؟ فقال: لئلا يكون لمخلوق عليه حق

QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r3.claim: Mujahid cites the metaphor of a unique pearl without peer: the Prophet was singular in nobility, then God supported him through protective companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:6/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد: هو من قول العرب: درة يتيمة

QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r1.claim: The sura recalls God's care, affection, and gifts from the Prophet's earliest days so he can relive divine mercy, intimacy, and tenderness.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r1.anchor: ليستحضر في خاطره جميل صنع ربه به ، ومودته له ، وفيضه عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r2.claim: God took the Prophet in as an orphan, drawing hearts to care for him, including his uncle Abu Talib despite Abu Talib not sharing his religion.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:6/r2.anchor: وعطف عليك القلوب حتى قلب عمك أبي طالب وهو على غير دينك

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r1.claim: The verse answers an earlier assurance: God cared for Muhammad when weak and orphaned, raised him greatly, and therefore will not abandon him now.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r1.anchor: كانت طاعاتك في ذلك الوقت أكرم أم الساعة ؟ فلا بد من أن يقال

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r2.claim: Here wajada means to know, with Muhammad and an orphan as the two objects: God knew him orphaned and sheltered him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r2.anchor: المنصوبان مفعولا وجد والوجود من الله ، والمعنى ألم يعلمك الله يتيما

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r3.speaker: أهل الأخبار
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r3.claim: They report that Muhammad's father died before his birth, his mother when he was six, and his grandfather two years later when he was eight.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن عبد المطلب فيما ذكره أهل الأخبار توفي وأم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حامل به

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r4.claim: Abu Talib then raised and supported Muhammad until his mission; the author says he never again appeared an orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r4.anchor: فكان أبو طالب هو الذي يكفل رسول الله بعد جده إلى أن بعثه الله للنبوة

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r5.speaker: أبو طالب
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r5.claim: In a report to al-Abbas, Abu Talib said he kept Muhammad beside him constantly, guarded him, and even placed him in his own bed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r5.anchor: إني ضممته إلي فكيف لا أفارقه ساعة من ليل ولا نهار ؛ ولا أأتمن عليه أحدا

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r6.claim: Abu Talib recounted Muhammad's modesty, fragrant presence, and miraculous appearances in bed, and said he never lied or joined ignorant children's play.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r6.anchor: فرأيت الكراهة في وجهه لكنه كره أن يخالفني ، وقال : يا عماه اصرف بوجهك عني

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r7.speaker: أبو طالب
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r7.claim: Abu Talib recalled that Muhammad began meals invoking the One God and ended them praising God, unlike the family's usual practice.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#2/r7.anchor: وكان يقول في أول الطعام : بسم الله الأحد . فإذا فرغ من طعامه قال : الحمدلله

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r1.claim: A second interpretation takes yatim as a unique pearl: Muhammad was peerless among Quraysh, and God gave him Abu Talib as refuge.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r1.anchor: التفسير الثاني لليتيم : أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة ، والمعنى ألم يجدك واحدا في قريش عديم النظير فآواك ؟

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r2.claim: The reading fa-awā can mean either that God sheltered him or showed him mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r2.anchor: وقرىء فأوى وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه ، وإما من أوى له إذا رحمه

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r3.claim: Divine reminders of favors strengthen the Prophet and promise their continuation; Pharaoh's reminder was self-serving, asking why Moses would not serve him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r3.anchor: أن ذلك يحسن إذا قصد بذلك أن يقوي قلبه ويعده بدوام النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r4.claim: God's promise to complete His favor resembles a sound pregnancy brought to term: abandoning the work of nurturing would be blameworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r4.anchor: وامتنان الله بزيادة نعمه ، كأنه يقول : مالك تقطع عني رجاءك ألست شرعت في تربيتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r5.claim: He contrasts a former community whose fourth was a dog with Muhammad's community, whose private conversations have God as the fourth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r5.anchor: نظيره ما قاله بعضهم : { ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم } ( الكهف : 22 ) في تلك الأمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.claim: Repaying benefaction is a lifelong, weightier debt than a financial loan; since God's gifts cannot be repaid, the servant should extend the same care to orphans and needy seekers and remember God's favor.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.anchor: فكأن العبد يقول : إلهي أخرجتني من العدم إلى الوجود بشرا سويا ، طاهر الظاهر نجس الباطن

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.claim: The practical answer to unrepayable divine gifts is to shelter orphans, guide and aid God's servants, and continually remember that even this service depends on God's help.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.anchor: فيقول تعالى الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك ، كنت يتيما فآويتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r2.claim: God made him an orphan so he would understand orphans' needs and defend their rights; Joseph avoided eating his fill lest he forget the hungry.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r2.anchor: أحدها : أن يعرف قدر اليتامى فيقوم بحقهم وصلاح أمرهم ، ومن ذلك كان يوسف عليه السلام لا يشبع

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r3.claim: Another proposed wisdom is the shared designation of orphanhood, which would occasion special honor; a report also urges honoring a child named Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r3.anchor: وثانيها : ليكون اليتيم مشاركا له في الاسم فيكرم لأجل ذلك ، ومن ذلك قال عليه السلام : ( إذا سميتم

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r4.claim: Without parents to rely on, he depended on God from earliest childhood, like Abraham entrusting himself to God and Mary's answer that provision came from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r4.anchor: فسلب عنه الولدان حتى لا يعتمد من أول صباه إلى آخر عمره على أحد سوى الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r5.claim: An orphan's faults are publicly visible; God chose this condition so observers would find no flaw in Muhammad and no objection to his prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r5.anchor: ورابعها : أن العادة جارية بأن اليتيم لا تخفى عيوبه بل تظهر ، وربما زادوا على الموجود فاختار تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r6.claim: His orphanhood makes clear that his excellence came from God, since a father normally works to educate and discipline a child.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r6.anchor: وخامسها : جعله يتيما ليعلم كل أحد أن فضيلته من الله ابتداء لأن الذي له أب ، فإن أباه يسعى

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.claim: Orphanhood and poverty are usually deficiencies, so Muhammad's becoming the most honored despite both overturns custom and functions as a miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.anchor: وسادسها : أن اليتم والفقر نقص في حق / الخلق ، فلما صار محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام / مع هذين الوصفين

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.claim: Mentioning these circumstances keeps the Prophet mindful of them and prevents self-admiration.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r1.claim: The common āwā is the transitive quadriliteral; Abū al-Ashhab reads the intransitive triliteral awā.
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r1.anchor: العامة على " آوى " بألف بعد الهمزة رباعيا، من آواه يؤويه. وأبو الأشهب " فأوى " ثلاثيا

SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the triliteral may mean the same as sheltered, or mean showed mercy; a shepherd's use is cited for the first and poetry for the second.
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r2.anchor: وهو على معنيين: إما من " أواه " بمعنى آواه. سمع بعض الرعاة يقول: " أين آوي هذه

SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r3.claim: The shepherd's present-tense āwī proves the triliteral: the quadriliteral would have the form uʾwī; the resulting two hamzas are not merged for weight, as with tuʾwīhi.
SAMIN-DURR:93:6/r3.anchor: أنه لو كان من الرباعي لقال: " أؤوي " بضم الهمزة الأولى وسكون الثانية

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r2.claim: After his father died before his birth and his mother when he was six, the Prophet was successively cared for by his grandfather and uncle Abū Ṭālib, who protected him; Khadījah was also a refuge.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r2.anchor: After this he was under the guardianship of his grandfather,ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, until he died when the Prophet was eight years old.

TAB:93:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:93:7/r1.claim: In recounting God's favors, al-Tabari explains that God found Muhammad an orphan and gave him shelter and a home.
TAB:93:7/r1.anchor: ألم يجدك يا محمد ربك يتيما فآوى ،   يقول :  فجعل لك مَأْوًى تأوي إليه ،   ومنزلا تنزله

TAB:93:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:93:8/r4.claim: Qatada calls orphanhood, being astray, and poverty the conditions of the Messenger before God sent him.
TAB:93:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيما فآوَى وَوَجَدَك ضَالاّ فَهَدَى وَوَجَدَكَ عائِلاً فأغْنَى قال :  كانت هذه منازل رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v24p489/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r1.claim: God recalls that He gave the orphaned Muḥammad shelter and a place to live.
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r1.anchor: وذكر أنها في مصحف عبد الله: «ووجدك عديما فآوى»

TABRISI:93:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r2.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
TABRISI:93:5/r2.claim: Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads fa-āwā without lengthening.
TABRISI:93:5/r2.anchor: وعن أشهب العقيلي فأوى بغير مد

TABRISI:93:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5/r6.claim: Fa-āwā derives from “I sheltered him,” meaning I showed him mercy.
TABRISI:93:5/r6.anchor: وأما قوله فأوى فإنه من أويته أي رحمته

TABRISI:93:5-7/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5-7/r3.claim: God sheltered the orphaned Prophet first through his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and then his uncle Abū Ṭālib, who loved and raised him.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r3.anchor: فآواه الله بأن سخر له أولا عبد المطلب ثم لما مات عبد المطلب قيض له أبا طالب

TABRISI:93:5-7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5-7/r4.claim: The Prophet's father may have died before his birth or soon after; his mother died when he was two and his grandfather when he was eight, leaving him with Abū Ṭālib.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r4.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مات أبوه وهو في بطن أمه

TABRISI:93:5-7/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r5.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:93:5-7/r5.claim: When asked why the Prophet was orphaned, al-Ṣādiq replied that no created being should have a claim over him.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r5.anchor: وسئل الصادق ع لم أوتم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبويه فقال لئلا يكون لمخلوق عليه حق

TABRISI:93:5-7/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5-7/r6.claim: Alternatively, yatīm means unmatched in honor and virtue, so God sheltered him close and selected him for prophecy; the source cites a pearl without equal.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r6.anchor: أن يكون المعنى ألم يجدك واحدا لا مثل لك في شرفك وفضلك

TABRISI:93:5-7/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r7.speaker: الماوردي
TABRISI:93:5-7/r7.claim: Al-Māwardī says God made the Prophet a refuge for orphans and protector of humanity after he himself was orphaned and protected.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r7.anchor: جعلك مأوى للأيتام بعد أن كنت يتيما وكفيلا للأنام بعد مكفولا عن الماوردي

THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.claim: They report that Jews asked about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills,” and revelation paused.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح

ASAD-NOTES:93:5#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:93:5#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:93:5#n3/r1.claim: The orphan reference may recall Muhammad's father's death before his birth and his mother's death when he was six; more broadly, everyone is created and resurrected alone.
ASAD-NOTES:93:5#n3/r1.anchor: Possibly an allusion to the fact that Muhammad was born a few months after his father's death

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r1.claim: In a report from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, God reminds the Prophet of earlier favors and he affirms them, including shelter as an orphan and the blessings in 94:1–4.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r1.anchor: فقال تبارك وتعالى: ألم أجدك يتيما فأويتك، وضالا فهديتك، وعائلا فأغنيتك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, God brought the Prophet into his uncle Abū Ṭālib's care until adulthood; Muqātil similarly says his uncle raised him and covered his expenses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد فضمك إلى عمك أبي طالب حتى صرت رجلا (¬3)، وقال مقاتل: ضمك إلى عمك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r3.claim: The Prophet was orphaned young when both parents died, without inherited money or shelter, and God placed him with his uncle, who raised him well.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p108/r3.anchor: والمعنى ألم نجدك يتيما صغيرا حين مات أبواك، ولم يخلفا لك مالا، ولا مأوى، فضمك إلى عمك

WAHIDI-QT:93:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:93:6/r1.claim: When Muhammad's parents died, he was an orphan without money or shelter; his uncle Abu Talib took him in, supported, and raised him.
WAHIDI-QT:93:6/r1.anchor: { ألم يجدك يتيما } حين مات أبواك ولم يخلفا لك مالا ولا مأوى { فآوى } فآواك إلى عمك أبي طالب وضمك إليه حتى كفلك ورباك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r1.claim: When Muhammad's parents died, they left him neither wealth nor shelter; God sheltered him with his uncle Abu Talib, who raised him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r1.anchor: حين مات أبواك ولم يخلفا لك مالا ولا مأوى { فآوى } فآواك إلى عمك

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r1.claim: Wājid derives from words for existence, finding, ecstasy, and wealth; God is possessor and agent of existence, knowledge, power, and wealth.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r1.anchor: Bunun asıl meşhur mânası varlık ve buluş ve zenginliktir

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r2.claim: Later scholars allow calling God mawjūd, though early scholars avoided it because it is a passive form used of created existence; revealed names include Wājid and al-Haqq.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r2.anchor: Menkul olan esmâ-i hüsnâda da “mevcud” ismi vârid olmayıp “Vâcid” ve “Hak” isimleri vârid olmuştur

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r3.claim: Exegetes often take wajada here as knowing: creaturely finding or knowing follows absence or ignorance, which cannot apply to God.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r3.anchor: burada Allah’a nisbet olunan وجد، يجد fiillerini de علم mânasına tefsir etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r4.claim: On that reading, the verse means that God knew the Prophet as an orphan and sheltered him.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r4.anchor: Buna göre mâna: “Seni bir yetim bilip yahut

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r5.claim: A possible but nonstandard reading makes the verb mean bringing into existence, with the Prophet as God's created object.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r5.anchor: Rabbin seni yetim olarak mevcud edip de barındırmadı mı?

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.claim: He prefers istifā, divine selection: finding a rare valuable thing represents choosing the Prophet from among creatures, a rhetorical emphasis repeated across all three verses.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.anchor: burada fikrimizce bunun en muvâfıkı bu fiillerin ıstıfâ mânasına olmasıdır

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r7.claim: Yatīm means an orphan left alone, and by extension a peerless precious object, as in the unmatched pearl called durr-i yatīm.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r7.anchor: Misli yok gayet kıymetli inciye “dürr-i yetîm” denilmesi de bundandır

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r8.claim: The Prophet was born fatherless: Abdullah died in Yathrib while the Prophet was a six-month fetus; his mother died when he was six and his grandfather when he was eight.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r8.anchor: o orada vefat etmişti. O sırada Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem henüz rahm-i mâderde altı aylık

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r9.claim: After the grandfather's death, Abu Talib took him in as guardian, cared for him attentively, and saw extraordinary qualities in him as a child.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r9.anchor: amcası Hazret-i Ebû Tâlib vasîsi olarak tekeffül edip yanına aldı, güzel baktı

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r10.speaker: أبو طالب
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r10.claim: In a report to Abbas, Abu Talib describes the Prophet's modesty, fragrant bedding, remembrance of God at meals, honesty, and avoidance of childish play as signs of great grace.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r10.anchor: Ben ondan ne bir yalan ne bir gülmek ne de câhillik görmedim

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r11.claim: An unattributed couplet says signs of noble character shine in the cradle, witnessing to the grandfather's happiness.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r11.anchor: فِي الْمَهْدِ يعرب عَنْ سَعَادَةِ جَدِّهِ أثَرُ النَّجَابَةِ سَاطِعُ البُرْهَانِ

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r12.claim: Āwā means to gather something to another and lodge or shelter it; God successively sheltered the Prophet after he was orphaned by father, mother, then grandfather, never abandoning him.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r12.anchor: “Îvâ” bir şeyi diğerine zammetmek, ircâ‘eylemek mânasından bir yurda

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r13.claim: A rhetorical reading hears yatīm also as the peerless pearl: God selected the unmatched Prophet and sheltered his heart in divine care.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r13.anchor: Seni halk içinde nazîrsiz, sadef-i imkânda misilsiz olarak ıstıfâ edip

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.claim: The three blessings show that each later state surpassed the earlier one, assuring the Prophet that this pattern will continue.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.anchor: Bunların mâkabline rabtıyla mâna şu olmuş oluyor: Görülüyor ki bunların hepsinde sonu evvelinden hayırlı olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r1.claim: Muhammad lost his father before birth and his mother at six; his grandfather and then uncle Abu Talib raised him, and Abu Talib defended him despite not openly declaring belief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r1.anchor: önce dedesi Abdülmuttalib’in, onun ölümünden sonra da amcası Ebû Tâlib’in himayesinde yetişmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r2.claim: After Abu Talib and Khadija died, the polytheists intensified their attacks; the surah consoles the Prophet by recalling God's past gifts and promising a better future.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r2.anchor: Bu sûrede Allah, o güne kadar peygamberine verdiklerini hatırlatarak teselli etmiş, geleceğinin daha iyi olacağını da müjdelemiştir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet regretted a request to receive other prophets' miracles; God reminded him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, enriched him, expanded his chest, and removed his burden.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r4.claim: The Prophet’s sheltering extended to many orphans; the author invokes the report that the caretaker of an orphan will be beside the Prophet in Paradise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r4.anchor: أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين وأشار إلى إصبعيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r7.claim: “Did He not find you” means “know you”; the Prophet’s father died when he was six months in the womb, and his mother when he was eight, after which Abū Ṭālib raised him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r7.anchor: ألم يجدك: يعلمك، يتيما: توفي أبوه عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو جنين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r8.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r8.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet was orphaned by both parents so he would owe no creature anything.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r8.anchor: وقيل لجعفر الصادق: لم يتم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أبويه؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports that yatīm can mean uniquely peerless, as a rare pearl, and interprets the verse as saying Muḥammad had no equal among Quraysh; Abū Ḥayyān dismisses the interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ومن يدع التفاسير أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r10.claim: The majority read fa-āwā as a quadriliteral verb; Abū al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads the triliteral fa-awā, meaning that God showed mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فآوى رباعيا وأبو الأشهب العقيلي: فأوى ثلاثيا، بمعنى رحم.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r1.claim: This question recalls the great favors from the Prophet's earliest life until revelation, using a known past favor to reassure him about the promised future; its separated interrogative denies the negative emphatically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r1.anchor: تعديل لما أفاض عليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من أول أمره إلى وقت النزول من فنون النعماء العظام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r2.claim: Finding can mean perceiving through outward senses, inward faculties, or intellect; when attributed to God it means pure knowledge, since He has no bodily organs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r2.anchor: وفي مفردات الراغب لوجود إضرب وجود بالحواس الظاهرة ووجود بالقوى الباطنة ووجود بالعقل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r3.claim: The best parse takes 'find' as knowing, with the Prophet as its object and 'orphan' as a second object; alternatively it means to find him in that state, but this cannot be literal of God, whose knowledge and decree precede it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r3.anchor: وقد فسره بعضهم هنا بالعلم وجعل مفعوله الأول الضمير ومفعوله الثاني يتيما وبعضهم بالمصادقة وجعله متعديا لواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r4.claim: An orphan is a child separated from his father before puberty, and sheltering means drawing someone under another's care.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r4.anchor: واليتم انقطاع الصبي عن أبيه قبل بلوغه والإيواء ضم الشيء إلى آخر يقال آوى إليه فلانا أي ضمه إلى نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r5.claim: The account says his father died while he was still a fetus, his mother when he was six, and his grandfather when he was eight; his uncle Abū Ṭālib then cared for him under the grandfather's instruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r5.anchor: روي أن عبد المطلب بعث ابنه عبد الله أبا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يمتار تمرا من يثرب فتوفي ورسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم جنين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r6.claim: In al-Zamakhsharī's report, Abū Ṭālib tells al-ʿAbbās that he guarded the child constantly; the boy modestly asked him to turn away while he undressed and appeared miraculously fragrant and soft, unlike ordinary children.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r6.anchor: وفي الكشاف ماتت أمه عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو ابن ثماني سنين فكلفه عمه وكان شديد الأعتناء بأمره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r7.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r7.claim: The same account says Muhammad alone began and ended meals with God's name and praise, never lied or laughed in a childish or ignorant manner, and did not join boys at play.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161/r7.anchor: وكنا لا نسمي على الطعام والشراب ولا نحمد وكان يقول في أول الطعام بسم الله الأحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r1.claim: Another interpretation says wet nurses initially rejected him, then one accepted and cared for him after receiving blessing through his companionship; Alusi prefers the orphaned-child explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r1.anchor: وقيل المعنى ألم يجدك يتيما أبتك المراضع فآواك من مرضعة تحنو عليك بأن رزقها بصحبتك الخير والبركة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls it a bizarre interpretation to read 'orphan' as a unique pearl meaning the Prophet was unmatched in Quraysh; Alusi says the notion would work better if he were described as unique among all creation, specially chosen for God's care.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r2.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير على ما قال الزمخشري أن يتيما من قولهم درة يتيمة والمعنى ألم يجدك واحدا في قريش عديم النظير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r3.speaker: أبو الأشعث
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Ashʿath reads فأوى with the simple verb; it may mean taking refuge or showing pity, with several cited verbal nouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p161#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو الأشعث فأوى ثلاثيا فجوز أن يكون من أواه بمعنى آواه وأن يكون من أوى له أي رحمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.claim: The Prophet recounts asking about other prophets' gifts; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, provision, an opened breast, and removal of his burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وودت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r7.claim: The Prophet was a poor child when both parents died, leaving neither money nor shelter; God gave him a home and placed him with his uncle Abu Talib, who raised and supported him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r7.anchor: يتيما صغيرا فقيرا حين مات أبواك ولم يخلفا لك مالا ولا مأوى، فجعلت لك مأوى تأوي إليه، وضمك إلى عمك أبي طالب

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r1.claim: Reminding the Prophet of past care assures him that God will continue to care for him despite any delay; يجد means “know” or “find,” with يتيم analyzed as second object or circumstantial predicate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r1.anchor: تعديد لما أنعم عليه تنبيها على أنه كما أحسن إليه فيما مضى

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.claim: A report promises acceptance among those for whom Muhammad may intercede and deeds equal to the number of orphans and petitioners for reciting al-Ḍuḥā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.anchor: من قرأ سورة والضحى جعله الله سبحانه وتعالى فيمن يرضى

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.claim: These reminders of earlier favors reassure Muhammad that God will not leave him: God sheltered the orphan, guided the bewildered, and enriched the needy.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.anchor: فهو تعالى يبث في نفس الرسول الطمأنينة ويثبت قلبه بلفته إلى ما أسبغ الله عليه في أولاه من نعم

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r2.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r2.claim: Al-Razi offers a metaphorical reading of yatim as a peerless pearl, meaning Muhammad was unmatched among Quraysh; God gave him Abu Talib as refuge.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r2.anchor: إنه من قولهم درة يتيمة، والمعنى: ألم يجدك واحداً في قريش عديم النظير

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r3.claim: Al-Razi also records the lighter reading fa-awā, understood as God showing mercy.

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rightly calls the pearl metaphor an invented interpretation and takes orphanhood in its ordinary sense of losing one's father, as do Abu Hayyan and al-Raghib.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r4.anchor: إن تفسير يتيم هنا بالدرة اليتيمة، من بدع التفاسير

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines the Quranic orphan as a child separated from his father before reaching puberty.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r5.anchor: اليتم - في آية الضحى - إنقطاع الصبي من أبيه قبل بلوغه.

BINTSHATI:v1p43/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r1.claim: The Quran pairs orphanhood with poverty in eleven passages.
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r1.anchor: ويلحظ فيه اقتران اليتم بالمسكنة في أحد عشر موضعاً:

BINTSHATI:v1p43/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r2.claim: Quranic contexts associate orphanhood with vulnerability: need, abuse of property, failure to honor, violent rejection, and oppression.
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r2.anchor: كما ذكر فيه من آثار اليتم: الجور، وأكل المال

BINTSHATI:v1p43/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r3.claim: Because Muhammad was orphaned at birth and lost his mother and grandfather too, God sheltered him from the social and psychological harms the Quran associates with orphanhood.
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r3.anchor: وقد ولد محمد يتيماً، ثم تضاعف يتمه بموت أمه وجده، لكنه تعالى نجاه من آثار اليتم

BINTSHATI:v1p43/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r4.claim: The unqualified verb āwā suggests divine safety, protection, and refuge, preparing the Prophet for guidance and the great message.
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r4.anchor: ترشيحاً بهذا الإيواء الإلهي - غير المقيد بمتعلق - إلى ما بعده

BINTSHATI:v1p43/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r5.claim: The Quran uses āwā fourteen times, consistently conveying a haven, protection, or refuge, literally or hopefully.
BINTSHATI:v1p43/r5.anchor: وقد جاء الفعل من {آوَى} في القرآن، أربع عشرة مرة، لا يخطئ الحس

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.claim: God's care did not restore Muhammad's dead father or fill his treasury; it preserved his character and prepared him psychologically for the message.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.anchor: وليست وقاية مادية ترد إليه أباه الذي مات قبل مولده، وتملأ خزانته بالمال

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.claim: Using the heart-verb wajada foregrounds the Prophet's inner state and emotional reassurance, rather than merely listing external circumstances.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.anchor: الفعل {وَجَدَ} وهو من أفعال القلوب ولم يقل مثلاً

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.claim: The omitted objects after sheltered, guided, and enriched are not merely for rhyme: the open wording can include both Muhammad and those helped through his mission.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.anchor: ونضيف إليها فائدة الإطلاق، فتحتمل: فآواك وآوى برسالتك اليتامى والمستضعفين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r1.claim: The Prophet was orphaned before birth when his father died and lost his mother at age eight, before reaching maturity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r1.anchor: من حين توفي أبوه وهو حمل وماتت أمه وهو ابن ثمان سنين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r2.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq explains that complete orphanhood ensured the Prophet owed no human being a parental debt.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r2.anchor: كما قال جعفر الصادق - حق لمخلوق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r3.claim: God found the Prophet an orphan and sheltered him; here finding means encountering someone and acting toward him accordingly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p456/r3.anchor: أي يصادفك أي يفعل بك فعل من صادف آخر

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن مخلد
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.claim: In a discussion about Abu Talib's praise of his nephew, Muslima cites God's reminders that Muhammad was orphaned, guided, and enriched.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.anchor: فقال مسلمة: ألم يقل الله {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى}

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.claim: He explains that Muhammad was orphaned by his parents' deaths and that the Arabs' former resources had dwindled to scarcity.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.anchor: فقال عبد الله: أما اليتيم فقد كان يتيما من أبويه وأما العيلة فكل ما كان بأيدي العرب إلى القلة

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r6.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r6.claim: He recounts that Abdullah died while seeking dates from Yathrib for Abd al-Muttalib, and Muhammad was born to Amina and raised by his grandfather.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r6.anchor: عن ابن شهاب رضي الله عنه قال: بعث عبد المطلب ابنه عبد الله يمتار له تمرا من يثرب فتوفي عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.claim: When the Prophet compared himself with earlier prophets' miracles, God reminded him of shelter, guidance, enrichment, an opened breast, removal of burden, and raised renown.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

DURR-FULL:v8p544/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r1.claim: In another report, the Prophet regretted a request comparing his gifts with those of other prophets, and God answered by reminding him of shelter as an orphan.
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سألت ربي شيئا وددت أني لم أكن سألته

TAB:93:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:93:6/r1.claim: God recalls His favor to Muhammad: He found him an orphan, gave him shelter, and provided a home to dwell in.
TAB:93:6/r1.anchor: ألم يجدك يا محمد ربك يتيما فآوى

BURHAN:v2p331/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p331/r1.claim: A report interrogative presses the addressee to admit a matter already established in their mind.
BURHAN:v2p331/r1.anchor: واما الثاني فهو استفهام التقرير والتقرير حملك المخاطب على الاقرار والاعتراف بأمر

BURHAN:v2p331/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r2.speaker: أبو الفتح
BURHAN:v2p331/r2.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ says report interrogation is not formed with هل.
BURHAN:v2p331/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح في الخاطريات ( 9 ) ولايستعمل ذلك بهل

BURHAN:v2p331/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.claim: A report question is semantically affirmative, so an explicit affirmative clause can coordinate with it, as in “Did He not find you an orphan, then shelter you, and find you astray, then guide you?”
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.anchor: فالاول كقوله ﴿ ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ﴾ 5 وقوله ﴿ ألم نشرح لك صدرك

BURHAN:v2p339/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p339/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p339/r2.claim: Some classify ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى and ألم نشرح لك صدرك as interrogatives for reminding the addressee.
BURHAN:v2p339/r2.anchor: وجعل بعضهم منه ﴿ ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ﴾ ﴿ ألم نشرح لك صدرك ﴾ 3

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.claim: Laf wa-nashr names two or more items and then corresponding details, either item by item or collectively, leaving listeners to match each detail to what fits.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: هو أن يذكر شيئان أو أشياء إما تفصيلا بالنص على كل واحد أو إجمالا بأن يؤتى بلفظ يشتمل على متعدد

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r6.claim: The command not to oppress the orphan corresponds to God having found the Prophet orphaned and sheltered him.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r6.anchor: فإن قوله ﴿ فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر ﴾ راجع إلى قوله ﴿ ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r18.claim: Wajada can mean see: Dāmghānī glosses the verse as asking whether God saw the Prophet as an orphan and sheltered him.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r18.anchor: ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك بمعنى ألم يرك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r1.claim: In common usage, dār names a plot enclosed by a building where someone lives, and by extension any place inhabited by a group.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r1.anchor: الدار في التعارف : اسم لكل عرصة دار عليها البناء يسكنها الإنسان . ثم يقال : لكل مكان حل به قوم : هو دارهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r2.claim: Dawārī is used for time because it turns people from one state to another; al-ʿAjjāj's line uses dawārī of time as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r2.anchor: ويقال للدهر : دواري ، لأنه يدور بالناس حالا عن حال ، وأنشدوا للعجاج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r3.claim: The Prophet compares a righteous companion to a perfumer: even if he does not give you fragrance directly, you still catch his scent; dārī means perfumer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r3.anchor: والداري : العطار . قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' مثل الجليس الصالح ، كمثل الداري

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r4.claim: Al-dārī can also mean a man who stays in his home and rarely leaves it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r4.anchor: والداري : الرجل المقيم في داره لا يكاد يبرحه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r5.claim: The Prophet asks which dūr of the Ansar are best; Ibn al-Jawzi explains dūr here as tribes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p291/r5.anchor: والدار : القبيلة . قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' ألا أنبئكم بخير دور الأنصار ' : أراد القبائل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.claim: The one who repels an orphan is described as denying religion, in contrast with God’s sheltering the Prophet when he was an orphan.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.anchor: دعَّ اليتيم في الآية تكذيباً بالدين. وفيما مَنَّ به الله تعالى على نبيه المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r3.claim: The unexpressed object of āwā allows several senses: God sheltered the Prophet, sheltered many through him, or sheltered others for his sake.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r3.anchor: احتملت المعاني آواك وآوى بك خلقاً كثيراً وآوى لك ولأجلك من آوى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r1.claim: Āwā is transitive by itself, as are hadā and aghnā; in 93:6 the omitted object leaves the construction open, unlike examples that state the person or object directly.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r2.claim: The ellipsis honors the Prophet by allowing several senses: God sheltered him, sheltered people through him and his teaching, and sheltered others for his sake; the same breadth applies to guidance and provision.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r2.anchor: والآية تحتمل المعاني الثلاثة آواك وآوى بك وآوى لك، وهداك وهدى بك خلقاً كثيراً وهدى لك.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r2.claim: The omitted object in فآوى allows several readings: God sheltered the Prophet, sheltered many through him, or sheltered others for his sake.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r2.anchor: احتملت المعاني آواك وآوى بك خلقاً كثيراً وآوى لك ولأجلك من آوى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r1.claim: Tafsir uncovers the intended sense of wording, including the meanings of individual words and explanations of obscure phrases or verses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r1.anchor: التفسير كشف المراد عن اللفظ، كشف مفردات، ما معنى هذه الكلمة؟ تفسير عبارة غير واضحة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r2.claim: Sound Qur’anic interpretation requires deep linguistic learning, which slight familiarity cannot replace, along with knowledge of hadith, Sunna, and occasions of revelation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1097/r2.anchor: ومن أول الضوابط التبحّر في علم اللغة ويقولون ولا تُغني المعرفة اليسيرة، ثم يذكرون أموراً تتعلق بالحديث والسُنّة وأسباب النزول

NASHR:v2p407/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r5.speaker: قيل
NASHR:v2p407/r5.claim: One explanation says the Prophet made takbir in joy over the blessings God enumerated, beginning with finding him an orphan and giving him shelter.
NASHR:v2p407/r5.anchor: وقيل كبر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فرحا

NASHR:v2p407/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r6.speaker: قيل
NASHR:v2p407/r6.claim: Another explanation says his takbir expressed gratitude to God for those blessings.
NASHR:v2p407/r6.anchor: وقيل شكرا لله تعالى على تلك النعم

NASHR:v2p407/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p407/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jazari suggests that the takbir expressed joy at God's gifts to the Prophet and his community, through which God would satisfy him in this life and the next.
NASHR:v2p407/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون تكبيره سرورا بما أعطاه الله عز وجل

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r1.claim: After the great promise, God recalls His favors to the Prophet during his upbringing.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r1.anchor: ولما وعده هذا الموعود الجليل ، ذكره بنعمه عليه في حال نشأته

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r2.claim: Here يجدك means that God knew or found him in the stated condition.

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r3.claim: The Prophet's father died while he was a six-month fetus; his mother died when he was eight, and Abu Talib then raised him well.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r3.anchor: توفي أبوه عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو جنين ، أتت عليه ستة أشهر وماتت أمه عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو ابن ثماني سنين

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r4.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq answers that the Prophet was orphaned from both parents so that no created being would have a claim upon him.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r4.anchor: وقيل لجعفر الصادق : لم يتم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أبويه ؟ فقال : لئلا يكون عليه حق لمخلوق

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also explains yatīm through the phrase for a unique pearl: the Prophet was unmatched in Quraysh, and God sheltered him.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ومن يدع التفاسير أنه من قولهم درّة يتيمة ، وأن المعنى : ألم يجدك واحداً في قريش عديم النظير فآواك

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r6.speaker: الجمهور وأبو الأشهب العقيلي
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r6.claim: The majority read quadriliteral فآوى; Abu al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli reads triliteral فأوى.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فآوى } رباعياً ؛ وأبو الأشهب العقيلي : فأوى ثلاثياً

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r7.claim: The triliteral form can mean to show mercy, as in the expression أويت لفلان.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r7.anchor: بمعنى رحم . تقول : أويت لفلان : أي رحمته

ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r8.claim: An unnamed poet's line is cited as evidence for the sense of showing mercy in أويت.
ABUHAYYAN:93:6/r8.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر : أراني ولا كفران لله أنه *** لنفسي قد طالبت غير منيل

ALUSI:93:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:6/r1.claim: The verse enumerates the great favors given from the Prophet's earliest life to revelation, using specific past favors to confirm future promises and reassure him; the clause is separated for this reason.
ALUSI:93:6/r1.anchor: طمأنينة وسروراً وانشراحاً وحبوراً ولذا فصلت الجملة

ALUSI:93:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:6/r2.claim: The interrogative hamza negates a negation and thereby affirms it in the strongest way, as though saying that God certainly found and sheltered him.
ALUSI:93:6/r2.anchor: والهمزة لإنكار النفي وتقرير النفي على أبلغ وجه كأنه قيل قد وجدك

ALUSI:93:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r3.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI:93:6/r3.claim: Al-Raḍī explains wajada as finding someone in a particular state; applied here to God, finding is figurative for knowledge through necessary association.
ALUSI:93:6/r3.anchor: ووجدته على ما قال الرضي بمعنى أصبته على صفة ويراد بالوجود فيه العلم مجازاً بعلاقة اللزوم

ALUSI:93:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:93:6/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes sensory, inward-faculty, and intellectual kinds of finding; finding attributed to God means pure knowledge, since God has no organs or instruments.
ALUSI:93:6/r4.anchor: وفي مفردات الراغب لوجود اضرب وجود بالحواس الظاهرة ووجود بالقوى الباطنة ووجود بالعقل

ALUSI:93:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:93:6/r5.claim: Some take wajada as knowledge, with the pronoun as its first object and yatīman as its second.
ALUSI:93:6/r5.anchor: وقد فسره بعضهم هنا بالعلم وجعل مفعوله الأول الضمير ومفعوله الثاني يتيماً

ALUSI:93:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:93:6/r6.claim: Others take wajada as finding, transitive to one object, and parse yatīman as a circumstantial accusative.
ALUSI:93:6/r6.anchor: وبعضهم بالمصادفة وجعله متعدياً لواحد ويتيماً حالاً

ALUSI:93:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:6/r7.claim: Literal discovery cannot apply to God because it would imply encountering something outside His knowledge and decree; the word must be figurative for His knowledge of it.
ALUSI:93:6/r7.anchor: أن المصادفة لا تصح في حقه تعالى لأنها ملاقاة ما لم يكن في علمه سبحانه وتقديره جل شأنه

ALUSI:93:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:6/r8.claim: An orphan is a child separated from his father before puberty; sheltering is joining one thing to another, so the verse means God sheltered the fatherless child through those who cared for him.
ALUSI:93:6/r8.anchor: واليتم انقطاع الصبي عن أبيه قبل بلوغه والإيواء ضم الشيء إلى آخر يقال آوى إليه فلاناً

ALUSI:93:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r9.speaker: روي
ALUSI:93:6/r9.claim: A report says ʿAbd Allāh died in Yathrib while the Prophet was a six-month fetus; after his birth his mother died when he was six, then his grandfather at eight, and Abū Ṭālib raised him under his father's charge.
ALUSI:93:6/r9.anchor: روي أن عبد المطلب بعث ابنه عبد الله أبا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمتار تمراً من يثرب فتوفي

ALUSI:93:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r10.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ALUSI:93:6/r10.claim: Al-Kashshāf instead says the Prophet's mother died when he was eight, after which his uncle cared for him closely until his mission.
ALUSI:93:6/r10.anchor: فكفله عمه وكان شديد الاعتناء بأمره إلى أن بعثه الله تعالى

ALUSI:93:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r11.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:93:6/r11.claim: Abū Ṭālib told al-ʿAbbās that the child kept his body covered, smelled like musk, sometimes vanished from his bed yet answered when called, invoked God at meals, and avoided lies, laughter, pagan customs, and children's games.
ALUSI:93:6/r11.anchor: قال يوماً لأخيه العباس ألا أخبرك عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بما رأيت منه فقال بلى

ALUSI:93:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r12.speaker: شاعر
