ALUSI:93:6/r12.claim: An unattributed poem says that even in the cradle he displayed the happiness of his grandfather and unmistakable signs of nobility.
ALUSI:93:6/r12.anchor: في المهد يعرب عن سعادة جده

ALUSI:93:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:6/r13.claim: Another explanation says wet nurses had refused the orphan, but God sheltered him with a nurse who came to love and care for him after receiving blessing through his companionship.
ALUSI:93:6/r13.anchor: وقيل المعنى ألم يجدك يتيماً أبتك المراضع فآواك من مرضعة تحنو عليك

ALUSI:93:6/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:93:6/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers the unusual reading that yatīm means a unique, peerless pearl: God found the Prophet unmatched among Quraysh and sheltered him.
ALUSI:93:6/r14.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير على ما قال الزمخشري أن يتيماً من قولهم درة يتيمة والمعنى ألم يجدك واحداً في قريش عديم النظير فآواك

ALUSI:93:6/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:6/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the pearl interpretation bizarre and says it would more fittingly mean that God found him peerless in all creation and selected him.
ALUSI:93:6/r15.anchor: والأولى عليه أن يقال ألم يجدك واحداً عديم النظير في الخليقة لم يحو مثلك صدف إلا مكان فآواك إليه

ALUSI:93:6/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:6/r16.speaker: أبو الأشعث
ALUSI:93:6/r16.claim: Abū al-Ashʿath reads the verb in the triliteral form fa-awā; it can mean that God sheltered him or had mercy on him, with the cited poetic line illustrating awā lahu.
ALUSI:93:6/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبو الأشعث فأوى ثلاثياً فجوز أن يكون من أواه بمعنى آواه وأن يكون من أوى له

ALUSI:93:8/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r16.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:93:8/r16.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests orphan means lacking a teacher, lost means lacking knowledge, and having dependents means the religious community needing guidance; God enriched the Prophet with revelation. Al-Ālūsī finds this strained.
ALUSI:93:8/r16.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

ALUSI:93:8/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the proposed allegory of orphanhood, misguidance, and dependents as deficiencies of teaching and knowledge is plainly strained.

ALUSI:93:8/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r18.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the verse endings.
ALUSI:93:8/r18.anchor: وحذف المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

ALUSI:93:8/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r19.claim: Another explanation says the omitted objects signal expansive generosity: God sheltered, guided, and enriched the Prophet and those connected with him; al-Ālūsī objects that the following fa-clauses resist this.
ALUSI:93:8/r19.anchor: وقيل ليدل على سعة الكرم والمراد آواك وآوى لك وبك وهداك ولك وبك وأغناك ولك وبك وظاهر الفاء مع تلك الأفعال نأبى ذلك

BAGHAWI:93:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:6/r1.claim: God recalls the Prophet's condition before revelation and reminds him of His favors.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r1.anchor: ثم أخبره الله عز وجل عن حالته التي كان عليها قبل الوحي ،   وذكر نعمه فقال جل ذكره :

BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking about gifts given to other men; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him. Other transmitters add that God expanded his breast and removed his burden.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI:93:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:6/r3.claim: When Muhammad was a poor child, his parents died without leaving property or shelter; God gave him refuge with his uncle Abu Talib, who raised and provided for him.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r3.anchor: معنى الآية : ألم يجدك يتيماً صغيراً فقيراً حين مات أبواك ولم يخلفا لك مالاً ولا مأوىً

BAYDAWI:93:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:6/r1.claim: This recounts a past favor to reassure the Prophet that God will continue to care for him even if help is delayed.
BAYDAWI:93:6/r1.anchor: تعديد لما أنعم عليه تنبيها على أنه كما أحسن إليه فيما مضى يحسن إليه فيما يستقبل وإن تأخر

BAYDAWI:93:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:6/r2.claim: Yajid means “know,” making yatīman its second object, or means “encounter,” with yatīman as a circumstantial accusative.
BAYDAWI:93:6/r2.anchor: من الوجود بمعنى العلم و يتيما مفعولك الثاني

BIQAI:93:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:6/r1.claim: After promising to raise the Prophet continually in rank and honor, God recalls the care with which He had already raised him.
BIQAI:93:6/r1.anchor: وعده بأنه لا يزال في كل لحظة يرقيه في مراقي العلا والشرف

BIQAI:93:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:6/r2.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BIQAI:93:6/r2.claim: The Prophet's father died while he was still a fetus and his mother when he was eight; being fully orphaned before puberty meant no created person had a claim over him, as Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says.
BIQAI:93:6/r2.anchor: يكون عليه - كما قال جعفر الصادق

BIQAI:93:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:6/r3.claim: God found him orphaned and took him into care.
BIQAI:93:6/r3.anchor: أي يصادفك أي يفعل بك فعل من صادف آخر

DURR:93:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR:93:6/r1.claim: In a discussion prompted by the verse, Muslama says Abu Talib would have recognized God’s blessing; Abdullah replies that even then Muhammad was already noble and had brought great good.
DURR:93:6/r1.anchor: فقال عبد الله : ويومئذ قد كان سيداً كريماً قد جاء بخير كثير

DURR:93:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR:93:6/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr explains that the Prophet was an orphan in that both his parents had died.
DURR:93:6/r2.anchor: فقال عبد الله : أما اليتيم فقد كان يتيماً من أبويه ،

DURR:93:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r4.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR:93:6/r4.claim: Ibn Shihab reports that Abd al-Muttalib sent his son Abd Allah to Yathrib for dates; Abd Allah died, and after Amina gave birth to Muhammad, his grandfather cared for him.
DURR:93:6/r4.anchor: عن ابن شهاب رضي الله عنه قال : بعث عبد المطلب ابنه عبد الله يمتار له تمراً من يثرب فتوفي عبد الله وولدت آمنة

DURR:93:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:93:6/r5.claim: The Prophet recalls asking for a favor he wished he had not requested; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, wealth, an opened breast, relief of burden, and raised renown, and he affirms each favor.
DURR:93:6/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته ، فقلت : قد كانت قبلي الأنبياء

DURR:93:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:93:6/r6.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s version, the Prophet wished he had not asked his Lord for something after comparing earlier prophets’ gifts, including Solomon’s wind and Moses; God then revealed this reminder of His favors.
DURR:93:6/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «سألت ربي شيئاً وددت أني لم أكن سألته

IBNASHUR:93:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r1.claim: The passage resumes as evidence that God's promise will come true, following the repeated care God showed the Prophet from the beginning of his life and through hardship.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r1.anchor: أي هو وعد جار على سنن ما سبق من عناية الله بك

IBNASHUR:93:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r2.claim: Repeated, consistent care cannot reasonably be coincidence, since coincidences do not recur in this way; its continuity shows God's intention.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r2.anchor: لأن شأن الصدف أن لا تتكرر فقد علم أن اطراد ذلك مراد لله تعالى

IBNASHUR:93:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r3.claim: This reminder gives the polytheists certainty that the promise will be fulfilled, perhaps turning them from obstinacy; it also comforts the Prophet and affirms God's favor to him.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r3.anchor: بأن ما وعده الله به محقق الوقوع قياسا على ما ذكره به

IBNASHUR:93:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r4.claim: The question is confirmatory; wajada means to find or encounter and takes one object, the second-person pronoun, while yatīman, ḍāllan, and ʿāʾilan are circumstantial accusatives.

IBNASHUR:93:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r5.claim: The wording pictures easing benefits for someone in difficulty as finding a distressed person looking for help or rescue.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r5.anchor: تمثيل لحالة تيسير المنافع للذي تعسرت عليه بحالة من وجد شخصا في شدة

IBNASHUR:93:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r6.claim: An orphan is a child whose father has died; the Prophet's father died while he was still in the womb or shortly after birth.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r6.anchor: الصبي الذي مات أبوه وقد كان أبو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفي

IBNASHUR:93:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:6/r7.claim: Īwāʾ literally means returning to a dwelling; here it figuratively means sponsorship and meeting needs, since God raised the Prophet with sound understanding and complete character despite the usual disadvantages of orphanhood.

IBNASHUR:93:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:6/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:93:6/r8.claim: The author cites the hadith 'My Lord disciplined me and made my discipline excellent' to contrast God's formation of the Prophet with upbringing by parents.
IBNASHUR:93:6/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث « أدبني ربي فأحسن تأديبي

IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because the preceding second-person pronouns make them understood; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.anchor: للعلم بها من ضمائر الخطاب قبلها ، وحدفها إيجاز

IBNATIYYA:93:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r1.claim: God reminds the Prophet of the stages through which divine favor raised him: losing his father and being cared for by his uncle Abū Ṭālib.
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r1.anchor: كان فقد أبيه وكونه في كنف عمه أبي طالب

IBNATIYYA:93:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq answered that the Prophet was orphaned of both parents so he would owe no creature a claim.
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r2.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق لم يتم النبي عليه السلام من أبويه ،   فقال لئلا يكون عليه حق لمخلوق

IBNATIYYA:93:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r3.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r3.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads fa-awā with a shortened form, giving it the sense of mercy.
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي «فأوى » بالقصر بمعنى رحم

IBNATIYYA:93:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:6/r4.claim: The shortened reading's verb is used in the expression aw aytu li-fulān, meaning I showed mercy to someone.

IBNKATHIR:93:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says Muhammad's father died while he was still in his mother's womb.
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r1.anchor: وذلك أن أباه توفي وهو حمل في بطن أمه

IBNKATHIR:93:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r2.claim: An alternate report says Muhammad's father died after he was born.
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r2.anchor: وقيل : بعد أن ولد ،   عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR:93:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r3.claim: His mother Āmina died when he was six; his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib cared for him until age eight, after which his uncle Abū Ṭālib took charge.
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r3.anchor: ثم توفيت أمه آمنة بنت وهب وله من العمر ست سنين

IBNKATHIR:93:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r4.claim: Abū Ṭālib supported and protected him after prophethood despite remaining an idolater; after his death shortly before the Hijra, God brought about the move to the Anṣār, who sheltered, defended and fought for him, all as divine care.
IBNKATHIR:93:6/r4.anchor: فكفله عمه أبو طالب . ثم لم يزل يحوطه وينصره ويرفع من قدره

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.claim: Qatada says these three conditions were the Messenger's circumstances before God sent him as a prophet.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَى

KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.claim: The opening enumerates God's favors from the Prophet's earliest upbringing, encouraging him to expect further favor and honor without losing patience or becoming distressed.
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.anchor: عدّد عليه نعمه وأياديه ،   وأنه لم يخله منها

KASHSHAF:93:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r2.claim: Wajada here means “know”; both following nouns are its objects, so the sense is “were you not an orphan?”
KASHSHAF:93:6/r2.anchor: من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم : والمنصوبان مفعولا وجد

KASHSHAF:93:6/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r3.claim: The Prophet's father died while he was a six-month fetus, his mother died when he was eight, and his uncle Abū Ṭālib cared for him and raised him well by God's kindness.
KASHSHAF:93:6/r3.anchor: وذلك أن أباه مات وهو جنين قد أتت عليه ستة أشهر

KASHSHAF:93:6/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r4.claim: Zamakhsharī rejects as an inventive interpretation taking yatīm like “a unique pearl,” meaning the Prophet was peerless among Quraysh.
KASHSHAF:93:6/r4.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أنه من قولهم

KASHSHAF:93:6/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r5.claim: The reading fa-āwā can mean he sheltered you, from āwā meaning āwāhu, or that he showed you mercy; a shepherd's usage attests the first verb.
KASHSHAF:93:6/r5.anchor: وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

MAWARDI:93:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:6/r1.claim: An orphan is one whose father has died; the Prophet lost his parents while young, was raised by his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and then by his uncle Abū Ṭālib.
MAWARDI:93:6/r1.anchor: واليتيم بموت الأب ،   وقد كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد أبويه وهو صغير ،   فكفله جده عبد المطلب

MAWARDI:93:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI:93:6/r2.claim: On the literal orphan reading, God gave the Prophet a home and a compassionate guardian to raise and support him after ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib died.
MAWARDI:93:6/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أي جعل لك مأوى لتربيتك ،   وقيمّاً يحنو عليك ويكفلك وهو أبو طالب بعد موت عبد الله وعبد المطلب ،   قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI:93:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI:93:6/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī instead says God gave the Prophet a home of his own and freed him from needing Abū Ṭālib's guardianship.
MAWARDI:93:6/r3.anchor: الثاني : أي جعل لك مأوى نفسك ،   وأغناك عن كفالة أبي طالب ،   قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI:93:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:6/r4.claim: Alternatively, yatīm can mean unique and without equal, as in the expression for a pearl with no match.
MAWARDI:93:6/r4.anchor: والوجه الثاني : أنه أراد باليتيم الذي لا مثيل له ولا نظير ،   من قولهم درة يتيمة ،   إذا لم يكن لها مثيل

MAWARDI:93:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:6/r5.claim: With the unique-person sense, God may have drawn the Prophet near and chosen him for His message.

MAWARDI:93:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:6/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:6/r6.claim: Alternatively, God made him a refuge for orphans and caretaker of people after he had been an orphan and cared for himself, recalling God's blessings.
MAWARDI:93:6/r6.anchor: الثاني : أن جعلك مأوى الأيتام بعد أن كنت يتيماً ،   وكفيل الأنام بعد أن كنت مكفولاً ،   تذكيراً بنعمه عليه ،   وهو محتمل

NASAFI:93:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:6/r1.claim: Listing earlier favors teaches the Prophet to measure future grace from past grace, expect good and more, and not lose patience or feel constricted.
NASAFI:93:6/r1.anchor: ثم عدد عليه نعمه من أول حاله ليقيس المترقب من فضل الله على ما سلف منه لئلا يتوقع إلا الحسنى وزيادة الخير

NASAFI:93:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:6/r2.claim: “Found” here means “knew,” and “you” and “orphan” are its two accusative objects.
NASAFI:93:6/r2.anchor: وهو من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم والمنصوبان مفعولاه

NASAFI:93:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:6/r3.claim: When his parents died, God sheltered him with his uncle Abū Ṭālib, who took him in, fostered him, and raised him.
NASAFI:93:6/r3.anchor: والمعنى ألم تكن يتيماً حين مات أبواك

QURTUBI:93:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:6/r1.claim: God recalls His favor: Muhammad's father had died, and God sheltered and supported him through his uncle Abu Talib.
QURTUBI:93:6/r1.anchor: عدد سبحانه مننه على نبيه محمد صلى اللّه عليه وسلم فقال : " ألم يجدك يتيما " لا أب لك قد مات أبوك . " فآوى " أي جعل لك مأوى

QURTUBI:93:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:6/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
QURTUBI:93:6/r2.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq answers that the Prophet was orphaned from both parents so that no created being would have a claim over him.
QURTUBI:93:6/r2.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق : لم أوتم النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم من أبويه ؟ فقال : لئلا يكون لمخلوق عليه حق

QURTUBI:93:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:93:6/r3.claim: Mujahid notes that Arabs call a pearl yatim when it has no equal; metaphorically, God found Muhammad unmatched in nobility and gave him protective companions.
QURTUBI:93:6/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد : هو من قول العرب : درة يتيمة ، إذا لم يكن لها مثل . فمجاز الآية : ألم يجدك واحدا في شرفك

RAZI:93:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r1.claim: Past care assures the Prophet that God will not abandon him after raising him from weakness to honor.
RAZI:93:6/r1.anchor: أن اتصاله بما تقدم هو أنه تعالى يقول

RAZI:93:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r2.claim: Wajada means to know; both accusatives are its objects, so God knew him as an orphan and sheltered him.

RAZI:93:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r3.speaker: أهل الأخبار
RAZI:93:6/r3.claim: The historians say ʿAbd Allāh died while Muḥammad’s mother was pregnant; she died when he was six, his grandfather two years later, and Abū Ṭālib then raised and supported him.
RAZI:93:6/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن عبد المطلب فيما ذكره أهل الأخبار توفي

RAZI:93:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r4.speaker: أبو طالب
RAZI:93:6/r4.claim: Abū Ṭālib told al-ʿAbbās he kept Muḥammad constantly close, found him modest and protected, and heard him invoke God at meals; he never saw him lie or join ignorant play.
RAZI:93:6/r4.anchor: قال أبو طالب يوما لأخيه العباس : ألا أخبرك

RAZI:93:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r5.claim: Rāzī says reports of the Prophet’s marvels, including the monk Baḥīrā story, are well known.
RAZI:93:6/r5.anchor: واعلم أن العجائب المروية في حقه من حديث بحيرى الراهب وغيره مشهورة

RAZI:93:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r6.claim: An alternative takes yatīm as a unique pearl: the Prophet had no peer among Quraysh, and Abū Ṭālib was the one with whom he could take refuge.

RAZI:93:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r7.claim: A reading has fa-awā, meaning either that God sheltered him or showed him mercy.
RAZI:93:6/r7.anchor: وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

RAZI:93:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r8.claim: Divine reminding strengthens the Prophet and promises lasting favor; Pharaoh’s reminder of raising Moses was blameworthy because it demanded service, while God promises to complete His bounty.
RAZI:93:6/r8.anchor: أن ذلك يحسن إذا قصد بذلك أن يقوي قلبه ويعده بدوام النعمة

RAZI:93:6/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r9.claim: Rāzī likens abandoning care before completion to losing a fetus: that is condemned and incurs compensation, so how could the Ever-Living Sustainer abandon His care?
RAZI:93:6/r9.anchor: أن الحامل التي تسقط الولد قبل التمام معيبة ترد

RAZI:93:6/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r10.claim: He contrasts a community whose fourth member is a dog with Muḥammad’s community, for which God Himself is the fourth.
RAZI:93:6/r10.anchor: في تلك الأمة ،   وفي أمة محمد

RAZI:93:6/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r11.claim: A debt of beneficence is harder to discharge than a financial debt: pardon does not cancel it, it lasts a lifetime, and great gifts are impossible to repay fully.

RAZI:93:6/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r12.claim: The response is to shelter orphans, guide people and provide for them as God did; even good works depend on God’s enabling and guidance.
RAZI:93:6/r12.anchor: الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك

RAZI:93:8/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r13.claim: Orphanhood taught the Prophet the worth and needs of orphans; Joseph did not eat his fill lest he forget the hungry.
RAZI:93:8/r13.anchor: أن يعرف قدر اليتامى فيقوم بحقهم وصلاح أمرهم

RAZI:93:8/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r14.speaker: يوسف عليه السلام
RAZI:93:8/r14.claim: Joseph explained that he feared eating his fill would make him forget the hungry.
RAZI:93:8/r14.anchor: كان يوسف عليه السلام لا يشبع .   فقيل له في ذلك : فقال أخاف أن أشبع فأنسى الجياع

RAZI:93:8/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r15.claim: An orphan shares the Prophet’s designation and should therefore be honored; a report urges honoring and making room for a child named Muḥammad.
RAZI:93:8/r15.anchor: ليكون اليتيم مشاركا له في الاسم

RAZI:93:8/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r16.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a child named Muḥammad should be honored and given room in the gathering.
RAZI:93:8/r16.anchor: قال عليه السلام :  " إذا سميتم الولد محمدا فأكرموه

RAZI:93:8/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r17.claim: Without parents to rely on, he depended on God alone; Rāzī compares this to Abraham’s trust and Mary’s answer that her provision came from God.
RAZI:93:8/r17.anchor: من كان له أب أو أم كان اعتماده عليهما

RAZI:93:8/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r18.claim: Since an orphan’s flaws are exposed and may be exaggerated, orphanhood made everyone scrutinize the Prophet; finding no fault left no objection to his appointment.
RAZI:93:8/r18.anchor: أن العادة جارية بأن اليتيم لا تخفى عيوبه بل تظهر

RAZI:93:8/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r19.claim: Orphanhood showed that the Prophet’s excellence came directly from God, since parents can teach and discipline a child.
RAZI:93:8/r19.anchor: جعله يتيما ليعلم كل أحد أن فضيلته من الله ابتداء

RAZI:93:8/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r20.claim: Orphanhood and poverty are disadvantages among people; his supreme rank despite both reverses expectations and is miraculous.
RAZI:93:8/r20.anchor: أن اليتم والفقر نقص في حق الخلق

RAZI:93:8/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r22.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r22.claim: A report has the Prophet ask for privileges given to Abraham, Moses, David and Solomon; God recalls these favors, opening his breast, raising his mention, removing his burden, giving him al-Baqara’s closing verses, and offering friendship as with Abraham.
RAZI:93:8/r22.anchor: سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أسألها

RAZI:93:8/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r23.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:93:8/r23.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that prophets would not ask this without permission, so the report cannot plausibly portray the Prophet asking and God responding with a reprimand.
